extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, journalists and policymakers seeking country-level comparisons of censorship, press freedom, and internet filtering
extracted.subtask_description: A global Wikipedia article compiling country-by-country data on censorship, press freedom, and internet filtering using third‑party indices and classifications. The page presents a sortable table and maps summarizing multiple freedom/censorship metrics for countries, former states, disputed territories, sub-units and regional organisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom House (FH) Freedom of the Press report
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom House 'Freedom of the Press' score: 10 is most free, 99 is least free. Score ranges used in the table: 10 to 30 = Free; 31 to 60 = Partly free; 61 to 99 = Not free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a numeric country score (column labelled 'FH Free press report (2012)' in the table). The article cites the Freedom of the Press data (example year referenced: 2012) and also shows a 2015 Freedom of the Press classification map. The numeric direction is explicit: lower = more free, higher = less free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporters Without Borders (RWB) Press Freedom Index
rubrics_metrics.description: RWB Press Freedom Index numeric scale: 6 is most free, 85 is least free. Ranges and labels shown: 6.00–12.99 = Good situation; 13.00–24.99 = Satisfactory situation; 25.00–36.49 = Noticeable problems; 36.50–55.29 = Difficult situation; 55.30–85 = Very serious situation; — = Not rated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a numeric country score (column labelled 'RWB Press freedom index (Jan 2013)'). The article also uses these bands in the Press Freedom Index map (2014). Lower numeric values indicate better press freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenNet Initiative (ONI) filtering classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: ONI classification codes for observed filtering: 'ne' = No evidence of filtering; 'sus' = Filtering suspected, but unconfirmed; 'sel' = Selective filtering observed; 'sub' = Substantial filtering observed; 'per' = Pervasive filtering observed; 'nd' = No data (does not indicate no censorship or no filtering); '—' = Not classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONI classifications are shown in the table (example year referenced: 2012) and used per filtering type (political/social/security/tools). The article notes ONI focuses on technical filtering and, due to legal concerns, does not check for filtering of child pornography (so 'nd' or absence of a code does not imply absence of censorship).

rubrics_metrics.name: ONI filtering dimensions (political / social / security / tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: The table includes separate ONI columns for types of filtering: political filtering, social filtering, security filtering, and tools filtering; each cell uses the ONI classification codes (ne, sus, sel, sub, per, nd).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four ONI dimensions indicate which kinds of content or technologies are subject to filtering in each country (e.g., political vs social content). Entries may differ across dimensions for the same country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom on the Net / Internet censorship & surveillance classifications (Freedom House 2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: Map/classification categories summarizing internet censorship and surveillance by country (Freedom on the Net 2018): Pervasive; Substantial; Selective; Little or none; Not classified / No data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for an overall summary map of internet censorship and surveillance; comes from Freedom House's 'Freedom on the Net' dataset (2018). These labels are qualitative summaries distinct from the numeric FH 'Freedom of the Press' score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of the Press map classifications (2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: Map legend categories for Freedom of the Press Report (2015): Not Free; Partly Free; Free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to color-code countries on the accompanying Freedom of the Press world map. These labels correspond to FH score bands (e.g., Free/Partly Free/Not Free).

rubrics_metrics.name: Press Freedom Index map classifications (2014)
rubrics_metrics.description: Map legend categories for Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index (2014): Very serious situation; Difficult situation; Noticeable problems; Satisfactory situation; Good situation; Not classified / No data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to color-code the RWB Press Freedom map. These qualitative labels map to numeric RWB score ranges (see RWB Press Freedom Index entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table scope and entity inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The table collects information on censorship, internet censorship, freedom of the press, freedom of speech, and human rights by country and presents it in a sortable table. In addition to countries, the table includes former countries, disputed countries, political sub-units within countries, and regional organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines what entities appear in the dataset (not only sovereign states). Users should expect entries for territories, disputed areas, historical regimes and regional bodies in addition to contemporary countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 'More information' link codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Legend for 'More info' column link markers: 'c' = Link to Censorship in [country] article; 'i' = Link to Internet censorship in [country] article; 'p' = Link to Freedom of the press or Freedom of speech in [country] article; 'h' = Link to Human rights in [country] article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These single-letter markers indicate which related articles are available for each country entry and provide pointers to deeper, topic-specific coverage beyond the summary table.
